context: Reverse-osmosis desalination plants force saline feedwater under high hydraulic pressure through semi-permeable polymer membranes that reject dissolved salts while allowing water molecules to pass. Over time, suspended solids, organic matter, and mineral scale accumulate on the membrane surface—a process known as fouling—which reduces permeate flux and increases required feed pressure. Pretreatment filtration, antiscalant dosing, and periodic membrane cleaning help sustain water output and extend membrane lifespan.
